pattern-selector.why: the design was chosen on purpose: a PreToolUse gate plus a load-state over a versioned router, rejecting a finish-only check and an auto-inject-and-allow that would make 'loaded' meaningless.
pattern-selector.what: chose the edit-time gate + per-session load-state + versioned router (single-purpose modules in always-on/), recorded in ADR-0098 with the options and the rejected ones.
quotes: the structure that fits the forces this system will actually face, chosen on purpose

architectural-decision-records.why: the decision (hold a source edit until select + load, with a versioned router and a compaction reload) is recorded in the same change.
architectural-decision-records.what: added docs/adr/0098-edit-time-select-load-gate.md (context, three options, decision, consequences with honest limits), the records schema doc, and a CHANGELOG entry.
quotes: Every architecturally significant change ships with an ADR in the same unit of work

bdd-comprehensive-testing.why: the eleven issue behaviors (edit held before selection, every skill gets a verdict, router-adds-required, load states, reload after compaction, no self-waive) are enumerated as scenarios, stored, logged, and run on the harness.
bdd-comprehensive-testing.what: added two Rules and eleven @audience:agent scenarios across the two always-on feature files with a step file driving the real scripts, refactored the shared selection Given, regenerated the datastore, and appended the coverage log.
quotes: These are not optional and not left to judgment.

comprehensive-test-strategy.why: the gate, validators, router, and load-state scripts are proven at the lowest layer that can catch the bug: unit/integration tests spawning the real scripts.
comprehensive-test-strategy.what: added test/routing-lib.test.mjs (a test per rule), test/check-task-plan.test.mjs, test/edit-gate.test.mjs, and test/load-state.test.mjs covering the accept path and every HOLD/deny/clear path.
quotes: Test at the lowest level that can catch the bug

verifiable-quality-gates.why: the edit-gate and validators are themselves checks, so they must be proven able to fail: their tests flip when the gate is neutralized.
verifiable-quality-gates.what: the four test files are discriminating: against a no-op gate/validator (always exit 0) every HOLD/deny flips, the reload test pins that skills are CLEARED not falsely marked loaded, and the per-rule router tests pin each mapping.
quotes: test must FAIL when the check is replaced by a no-op

skeptical-audit.why: the gate enforces evidence in code - 'loaded' means the current text was genuinely read (hash-matched), not recalled - and the ADR carries evidence states and named limits.
skeptical-audit.what: the load check refuses a skill whose current text was not delivered (stale hash does not count); the ADR names the limits (hooks fail open so each must exit non-zero; Bash is best-effort; a real SKILL.md exceeds the additionalContext cap so bodies cannot be re-inlined).
quotes: If you cannot attach all three, you do not assert it

owasp-secure-coding-bdd.why: the hooks parse untrusted payloads and resolve skill files from selection/payload-supplied names, so they are threat-modeled against path traversal and injection.
owasp-secure-coding-bdd.what: skill names are rejected for '.'/'..'/path separators before any join in check-task-plan, record-load, and reload-skills; payloads are parsed as JSON never eval'd; the edit-gate fails closed (deny) on any error so a crash cannot bypass it; covered by the test files.
quotes: Each per-sheet file states the real attack the control stops

judge-arch.why: a fresh-context review ran on the diff before this receipt; it raised four findings (two high, two medium), all fixed and pinned, and is recorded in the arch-review log.
judge-arch.what: dispatched the four-questions review to a general-purpose subagent; fixed the false-loaded reload, the compact hook wired under the wrong event, the edit-gate fail-open after parse, and the over-broad Bash matcher; recorded in docs/arch-reviews/log.jsonl.
quotes: These are not optional and not left to discretion. Every review does all of them.

enterprise-architecture-standards.why: no new system or data architecture, schema, service, or scaling surface; the boundary/ownership/dependency/error review for these enforcement scripts is carried by judge-arch (applied) and the design by pattern-selector (applied).

arch-encode.why: no new greppable arch-gate rule was encoded; the enforcement is a runtime gate plus discriminating tests, not a static lint over source.

release-deployment-safety.why: no deploy, release, rollout, cutover, migration, or feature flag; nothing about what runs in production changes.

sre-operational-readiness.why: no running service, endpoint, SLO, alert, or on-call surface; these are local hook scripts invoked by Claude Code.

compliance-data-lifecycle.why: no personal or regulated data, consent, retention, or data migration; the load-state holds skill names and file hashes only.

universal-accessibility-wcag.why: no UI; hook scripts with no rendered interface.

universal-browser-device-support.why: no browser- or device-facing code; Node hook scripts.

usability-ux-universal-design.why: no user-facing UI; the hooks' developer-facing messages name the cause and the fix, following the repo's existing checker-message style.
